Soojin — quick read and feasibility notes below. Attaching a short methodology summary that maps to Helios' spreadsheet (see sandbox-run-methodology.md stub attached to this thread).

High-level feasibility: yes — we can reproduce the mix in a dedicated sandbox with the following approach.

Runbook summary (concise):
- Workload driver: k6-based driver configured to replay request distribution by endpoint and prompt-length buckets from sandbox-traffic-specs.csv. We will seed with a synthetic but representative corpus to avoid PII leakage.
- Models / variants: run two variants — the production quantized open model (v1-q4b) and an LLM-lite variant for fallback. Each run will be tagged so we can surface model-level throughput/latency.
- Metric collection: token-level latencies collected from the runtime tracing hooks, aggregated into p50/p95/p99 by request size and by model. GPU telemetry via Prometheus exporters; NVML sampling for GPU utilization and power.
- Tail analysis: collect per-request metadata for requests > 2s; correlate with sequence length, cache-miss, and model fallback events.

Constraints / notes:
- Peak 1.2k RPS sustained across mixed models will need a reserved 8xA100 equivalent for a full-day run; if customer prefers hosted sandbox (shared capacity) we will run a scaled-demo at 50% peak and model extrapolation is provided.
- Raw logs: we will provide run-level logs with IPs and tokens redacted; request/response hashes will be included for validation.

Artifacts we will deliver: sandbox-run-methodology.md (text), raw-logs-redacted.tar.gz (attachment stub), redwood-lab-evidence-report-Helios.pdf (narrated results), aggregated-metrics.csv.

Estimated timeline: dry-run in 48 hours; full evidence bundle in 5 business days after dry-run signoff (same as Soojin's note).

Attachments referenced: sandbox-run-methodology.md (methodology), redwood-lab-evidence-report-Helios.pdf (final report stub)
